names.meaning: The One Most ready to appreciate and reward abundantly

blocks.text: The Name Ash-Shakoor The One Most ready to appreciate and reward abundantly is found in four places in the Qur'aan,
That He may pay them their wages in full, and give them (even) more, out of His Grace. Verily! He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Ready to appreciate (good deeds and to recompense).
And they will say: "All the praises and thanks be to Allah, Who has removed from us (all) grief. Verily, our Lord is indeed Oft-Forgiving, Most Ready to appreciate (good deeds and to recompense).
Verily, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Ready to appreciate (the deeds of those who are obedient to Him).
And Allah is Most Ready to appreciate and to reward, Most Forbearing
Ash-Shaakir The Appreciative occurs in two places,
then verily, Allah is All-Recogniser, All-Knower.
And Allah is Ever All-Appreciative (of good), All-Knowing.

All these six places where the two Names occur are in the context of Allaah giving by rewarding the obedient people, giving and multiplying the rewards and increasing them in grace. This is what clarifies to us the meaning of these two Names.
• The One who does not allow a good deed by a good doer to be lost instead He multiplies the reward without account.
• The One who accepts small good deeds and rewards them with many rewards, abundant giving and vast gifts.
• The One who multiplies the deeds of the sincere people without measure.
• He is appreciative of those who are grateful.
• He remembers those who remember Him.
• Whoever draws close to Him by a hand span, He draws close to him by an arm's length. Whoever comes close to Him by an arm's length He draws close to him by a fathom.
• Whoever comes with a good deed He increases it in goodness and He gives him from Himself a mighty reward.

In the previous aayaat Al-Ghafoor The Forgiving and Ash-Shakoor The One Most ready to appreciate and reward abundantly are combined. So He forgives all sins no matter how great. He does not make a sin too great to be forgiven. Ash-Shakoor The One most ready to appreciate every deed even if it be small, even if it is the weight of a seed. Due to this it is not allowed for a Muslim to despair of Allaah's forgiveness for sins no matter how great. Just as it is not allowed to look down upon any good deed no matter how small because indeed the Lord is Ghafoor Forgiving, Shakoor Appreciative.

keyPoints: Ash-Shakoor is found in four places in the Qur'aan and Ash-Shaakir in two places.
All six places are in the context of Allaah rewarding the obedient, multiplying their rewards and increasing them in grace, which clarifies the meaning of these two Names.
Ash-Shaakir is the One who does not let a good deed be lost, accepts small good deeds and rewards them abundantly, and multiplies the deeds of the sincere without measure.
Whoever draws close to Him by a hand span, He draws close to him by an arm's length, and whoever comes close by an arm's length, He draws close by a fathom.
Al-Ghafoor and Ash-Shakoor are combined: He forgives all sins no matter how great and appreciates every deed even if small, so a Muslim must not despair of forgiveness nor look down on any good deed.

recall.q: What does Ash-Shakoor mean, and how many times is it found in the Qur'aan?
recall.a: The One Most ready to appreciate and reward abundantly; it is found in four places.

recall.q: What does Ash-Shaakir mean, and how many times does it occur?
recall.a: The Appreciative; it occurs in two places (Baqarah 2:158 and Nisaa 4:147).

recall.q: What is the common context of all six places where these two Names occur?
recall.a: Allaah giving by rewarding the obedient people, giving and multiplying the rewards and increasing them in grace.

recall.q: Which Name is combined with Ash-Shakoor in the aayaat, and what lesson does the author draw?
recall.a: Al-Ghafoor; so a Muslim must not despair of Allaah's forgiveness no matter how great the sin, nor look down upon any good deed no matter how small.
